subject: science
title: How sound is made and travels

cards.back: Something we hear. It is made by vibrations.
cards.say: sound. Something we hear. It is made by vibrations. A bell makes a sound.

cards.back: A quick movement backwards and forwards.
cards.say: vibration. A quick movement backwards and forwards. A plucked guitar string vibrates.

cards.back: A vibration.
cards.say: What makes a sound? A vibration.

cards.front: How can you feel a vibration when you speak?
cards.back: Put your fingers on your throat while you talk.
cards.say: How can you feel a vibration when you speak? Put your fingers on your throat while you talk.

cards.back: The strings.
cards.say: What vibrates in a guitar? The strings.

cards.back: The drum skin.
cards.say: What vibrates in a drum? The drum skin.

cards.back: Your vocal cords.
cards.say: What vibrates when you speak? Your vocal cords.

cards.back: Yes, for example through a wall or a table.
cards.say: Does sound travel through solids? Yes, for example through a wall or a table.

cards.back: Yes. You can hear sounds under water.
cards.say: Does sound travel through liquids? Yes. You can hear sounds under water.

cards.back: Yes. Sound travels through air to our ears.
cards.say: Does sound travel through gases? Yes. Sound travels through air to our ears.

cards.front: Does sound travel through a vacuum (empty space)?
cards.back: No. Sound needs a material to travel through.
cards.say: Does sound travel through a vacuum, which is empty space? No. Sound needs a material to travel through.

cards.back: Vibrations travel through the air to our ear.
cards.say: How do we hear sounds? Vibrations travel through the air to our ear.

cards.front: Which part of the ear catches sounds?
cards.back: The outer ear.
cards.say: Which part of the ear catches sounds? The outer ear.

cards.back: A thin skin inside the ear that vibrates when sound reaches it.
cards.say: eardrum. A thin skin inside the ear that vibrates when sound reaches it.

cards.front: Why can you hear a friend through a closed door?
cards.back: Sound vibrations pass through the door.
cards.say: Why can you hear a friend through a closed door? Sound vibrations pass through the door.

cards.front: Does sound travel faster in air or in a solid?
cards.back: In a solid.
cards.say: Does sound travel faster in air or in a solid? In a solid.

cards.front: Does sound travel faster than light?
cards.back: No. Light is much faster, so we see lightning before we hear thunder.
cards.say: Does sound travel faster than light? No. Light is much faster, so we see lightning before we hear thunder.

cards.back: A sound that bounces off a surface and is heard again.
cards.say: echo. A sound that bounces off a surface and is heard again. You can hear an echo in a cave.

cards.front: What do we need to hear a sound?
cards.back: A source, a material to travel through and a listener.
cards.say: What do we need to hear a sound? A source, a material to travel through and a listener.

cards.front: Why do astronauts need radios in space?
cards.back: There is no air in space for sound to travel through.
cards.say: Why do astronauts need radios in space? There is no air in space for sound to travel through.

cards.front: Why is a room with carpets less echoey?
cards.back: Soft materials absorb the sound.
cards.say: Why is a room with carpets less echoey? Soft materials absorb the sound.

cards.front: True or false: Sound is made when something is still.
cards.back: False. Sound is made by vibrations.
cards.say: True or false: Sound is made when something is still. False. Sound is made by vibrations.

cards.front: How could you show a drum is vibrating?
cards.back: Put grains of rice on the skin and tap. They bounce.
cards.say: How could you show a drum is vibrating? Put grains of rice on the skin and tap. They bounce.
